title: Guard a script’s inputs
goal: Guard script inputs and report failures predictably before declaring success.
challenge: Write a Bash checker accepting one readable regular file. Return 2 for argument count, 3 for missing/unreadable/non-file input, 4 for empty input and 5 when the exact READY record cannot be confirmed. Success prints ready: <path> and exits 0. Test failure cases; errors belong on stderr.

steps.explanation: Create a unique learner-owned guest workspace. Stop if creation or cd fails. Retain its printed path; variables do not survive disk Resume.
steps.expected: A fresh directory inside the guest home; no existing files are changed.

steps.command: printf '%s\n' READY > 'ready note.txt'; : > empty.txt; printf '%s\n' WAIT > wrong.txt
steps.explanation: Small fixtures make valid and invalid behavior observable.

Enter this bounded checker and save/exit:
#!/bin/bash
if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then printf 'usage: guarded FILE\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
input=$1
if [ ! -f "$input" ] || [ ! -r "$input" ]; then
  printf 'unreadable file\n' >&2; exit 3
fi
if [ ! -s "$input" ]; then
  printf 'empty file\n' >&2; exit 4
fi
grep -qx -- READY < "$input"; status=$?
if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
  printf 'READY check failed, grep status=%s\n' "$status" >&2; exit 5
fi
printf 'ready: %s\n' "$input"
steps.expected: Explicit argument/readability/content conditions; no set -e shortcut.

steps.command: bash -n guarded.sh; chmod u+x guarded.sh; timeout -k 2s 5s ./guarded.sh 'ready note.txt' > good.txt; printf 'good=%s\n' "$?" > status.txt
steps.explanation: Syntax and behavior are separate checks. Quoted argument preserves the space.

steps.command: timeout -k 2s 5s ./guarded.sh missing.txt > failed.txt 2> errors.txt; printf 'missing=%s\n' "$?" >> status.txt; timeout -k 2s 5s ./guarded.sh empty.txt >> failed.txt 2>> errors.txt; printf 'empty=%s\n' "$?" >> status.txt
steps.explanation: Neither existence nor successful syntax checks establish useful input.

steps.command: timeout -k 2s 5s ./guarded.sh wrong.txt >> failed.txt 2>> errors.txt; printf 'content=%s\n' "$?" >> status.txt; timeout -k 2s 5s ./guarded.sh >> failed.txt 2>> errors.txt; printf 'args=%s\n' "$?" >> status.txt; cat status.txt errors.txt
steps.explanation: Preserve the actual grep status in the error. A no-match and an I/O error both prevent success, without claiming they are the same cause.

hints: Which conditions must hold before a success message is justified?
Compare actual output, immediate exit status and resulting files. A syntactically valid command or script can still do the wrong thing.
Keep the original, verify a small intended change, and demonstrate rollback inside this workspace.
